en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-dou-sha-jing* (The Sūtra on the Buddha’s Enumeration), one fascicle,
translated by the Yuezhi Tripiṭaka Master Lokakṣema during the Later Han Dynasty.
The majestic spiritual power and grace of all Buddhas— of those of the past, future, and present— is likewise thus.
When the Buddha was in the kingdom of Magadha at the site of the Pure Dharma, that place was known as "Pure in Whatever is Asked.
When he first attained Buddhahood, its radiance was exceedingly bright.
The natural vajra-lotus is exceedingly vast in circumference.
There is a natural lion-throne upon which all Buddhas of the past have likewise sat; their deportment and ritual methods are no different.

Within the Dharma of ultimate characteristics, having already transcended the most extreme limits, the physical conduct of all Buddhas is entirely equal and complete; their clarity is such that there is no longer any obstruction.

It is the place of incalculable Buddhas, the place of incalculable Dharmas, the place of incalculable beings throughout the ten directions, and the place of incalculable Buddha-fields; it is that which has been produced by the Buddhas of the past, the future, and the present.
The bodhisattvas each came from different buddha-lands to the great assembly, their number being equal to the dust motes of ten buddha-fields;
one dust mote representing one bodhisattva—this was the limit.

All these Bodhisattvas, having been granted the stage of being in their final birth (*ekajātipratibaddha*), have all entered into the governance and peace of the people of the ten directions; they have all entered the locus of the Dharma; they have all entered the various lands of the ten directions; they have all entered the wisdom of *nirvāṇa* throughout the ten directions; they have all entered into the past lives of the worldly people of the ten directions; they have all entered the stage of the Bodhisattva who gradually deepens his progress; they have all entered into all dharmas of wisdom; they have all entered into internal and external dharmas; they have all entered into the dharmas that are unmoving and unshakable; and they have all entered into the dharmas of the past, future, and present.
The various bodhisattvas deliberated thus:
"The Buddha loves us and our like.
This was what the various bodhisattvas thought:
"Reveal to us all the buddha-fields, just as the Buddha dwells in his own sphere of activity.
Manifest to us all that we have heard; manifest to us the purity of all buddha-fields and manifest to us the purity of the Buddha-dharma."
"The Dharma taught by the Buddha has been made entirely visible to us;
the times of the formation and destruction of our buddha-fields have also been made fully visible to us."
"Manifest to us the time when all Buddhas arise and appear; manifest to us all that is virtuous and non-virtuous within our buddha-fields; and reveal everything that the Buddhas possess to us."

"Manifest to us the various lands of the ten directions; manifest to us the immeasurable teachings spoken by all Buddhas; manifest to us the ten stages of the bodhisattva’s dwelling; manifest to us the ten practices of the bodhisattva; manifest to us the *Sūtra on the Ten Dharma-Regrets* of the bodhisattva; manifest to us the ten grounds of the bodhisattva’s path; manifest to us the ten stabilizations of the bodhisattva; manifest to us the ten vows regarding the bodhisattva’s abodes; manifest to us the ten insights of the bodhisattva; manifest to us the thirteen samādhis of the bodhisattva; manifest to us the ten methods of flight of the bodhisattva; manifest to us the ten seals of the bodhisattva; manifest to us when the bodhisattvas all arrive by flight; and manifest to us the names of the Buddhas without end."
“At that time, the Buddha commanded me to protect all the people of the world, so that all the lands of the Buddhas in the ten directions might be entirely pure and free from defilement.
He revealed to me all that the Buddhas know—both existence and non-existence—and he revealed to me the roots of all evils, causing them all to become pure.”

"I shall explain all dharmas for you; I shall resolve all doubts and difficulties—I shall completely dispel all uncertainty and lead you all across to the other shore—so that all cravings may be severed."

“Reveal the place where my Buddha dwells; reveal the realm of my Buddha’s various dharmas; reveal my Buddha’s majestic spiritual power; reveal my Buddha’s conduct; and reveal my Buddha’s physical strength.”

"It manifests the four things that my Buddha does not need to guard; it manifests the place where my Buddha enters samādhi; it manifests the transformations performed by my Buddha and what they are for.
It manifests that there is no one who surpasses my Buddha; it manifests all the honorific titles of my Buddha, such that none can equal or reach them."
He manifests my Buddha’s faculties; he manifests my Buddha’s flight; he manifests my Buddha’s radiance; he manifests my Buddha’s wisdom; he manifests my Buddha’s four grounds of self-confidence.
The Buddha, fully knowing the thoughts in the minds of all the bodhisattvas, manifested his radiant majesty and spiritual power.
To the east, at an immeasurably distant buddha-field, there was a buddha named Aśvaghoṣa; that field was named Kṣemavatī.

The Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī came from this land accompanied by a multitude of bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms within the lands of the ten directions; they all came forward to pay homage to the Buddha and each sat upon a naturally formed lion throne within a lattice-canopied pavilion.
In the southern direction, at an immeasurably distant Buddha-field, there is a Buddha named Aniruddharāja; that field is called Lohitavana.

From that field came the Bodhisattva Buddhasiri together with a multitude of bodhisattvas—numbering as many as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields—who all came forward to pay homage to the Buddha and each sat upon a naturally formed lion throne within a lattice-canopied pavilion.
In the western direction, at an immeasurably distant buddha-field, there is a Buddha named Asita; that field is named Pāṭhāna.

From that field comes the Bodhisattva Rociśrī, accompanied by a multitude of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields. They all came forward to pay homage to the Buddha and each sat upon a natural lion throne within a lattice-canopied pavilion.
In the far north, beyond incalculable Buddha-fields, there is a Buddha named Ajita; his field is called Ghanavyūha.

From that field, the Bodhisattva Dānaśrī came together with a multitude of bodhisattvas—equal in number to the dust motes of ten Buddha-fields—and all approached to pay homage to the Buddha. Each sat upon a naturally arisen lion throne within a lattice-canopied pavilion.
In the far northeast, beyond incalculable Buddha-fields, there is a Buddha named Aśvanadraghota, and his field is named Upavana.

From that field, the Bodhisattva Guṇaśrī arrived together with a multitude of bodhisattvas—equal in number to the dust motes of ten Buddha-fields—and all came forward to pay homage to the Buddha, each sitting upon a naturally appearing lion throne within a lattice-canopied pavilion.
In the southeastern direction, at an immeasurably distant buddha-field, there is a Buddha named Ajantadhvaja; that field is called Gandhavatī.

From that field comes the Bodhisattva Nalinavimalaśrī, accompanied by a multitude of bodhisattvas as numerous as the atoms in ten buddha-fields. They all come forward to pay homage to the Buddha and each sits upon a naturally manifested lion throne within a lattice-canopied pavilion.
In the far southwest, beyond incalculable Buddha-fields, there is a Buddha named Utsada (郁沈墮大), and his field is named Rāvaṇa (羅憐洹).

The Bodhisattva Viśeṣamati (惟闍師利) came from that field together with a multitude of bodhisattvas—numbering as many as the dust motes in ten Buddha-fields—and all approached to pay homage to the Buddha, each sitting upon a naturally manifested lion throne within a cross-latticed canopy.
In the far northwest, beyond incalculable Buddha-fields, there is a Buddha named Aparājita, whose land is called Vairaṇyā.

From that land came the Bodhisattva Dharmasiri together with a multitude of bodhisattvas, as numerous as the atoms in ten Buddha-fields. They all came forward to pay homage to the Buddha and each sat upon a natural lion throne within a lattice-canopied pavilion.
In an extremely distant and incalculable number of Buddha-fields below, there is a Buddha named Pāṇḍuravāsas; his field is named Pāṇḍubhūmi.

The Bodhisattva Ratnaśrī came from that field together with a multitude of bodhisattvas—equal in number to the dust motes of ten Buddha-fields—and all approached to pay homage to the Buddha, each sitting upon a naturally formed lion throne within a lattice-canopied pavilion.

In the far distance above, beyond the reach of calculation, there is a buddha-field where a buddha resides; that buddha is named Duose (Dharmavarṇa), and his field is named Qieti Shihuan (Caitraratha).

From that field, the bodhisattva Nabadhasiri arrived together with a multitude of bodhisattvas—numbering as many as the atoms in ten buddha-fields—and all came forward to pay homage to the Buddha, each sitting upon a naturally manifested lion throne within a lattice-canopied pavilion.
Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, sustained by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual power, surveyed all the bodhisattvas everywhere; having done so, he spoke these words of wisdom:
"This great assembly of bodhisattvas—how exceedingly joyful it is!"
One cannot further calculate the various Buddha-fields—the abodes where Buddhas dwell and all their locations;

nor can one calculate the various ways they are clothed in the Buddha-dharma—the Buddhas’ preaching of the Dharma, the majestic spiritual power of the Buddha-fields, the conduct of the Buddhas, the physical strength of the Buddhas, the virtues and evils of the Buddha-fields, and the incalculable qualities of the Buddha-dharma.
"For what reason?

The path taught in the Buddha-fields of the ten directions and those who are delivered and liberated throughout the ten directions—their dharmas are profoundly deep and boundless, like space, entirely without obstruction."
"For what reason?

In this Sahā world-system, there are various kinds of people on all four sides—each with different bodies, each with different names, each with different complexions, each with different heights, each with different lifespans, each with different physical forms, each with different thoughts, each with different intentions, and each with different voices—and yet each hears the voice of the Buddha."
"For what reason is this land named Pākasitī? Within its four directions, some call the Buddha by the name Śreṣṭha;

some call him Janma-māndhātṛ; some call him Ayanaṇḍita; some call him Śākyamuni; some call him Maudgalyāyana; some call him Droṇa; some call him Kuvakrānti; some call him Mahāśramaṇa; some call him Cūḍapanthaka; and some call him Citrapanthaka."
For those such as these in the four directions, each called upon the name of Śākyamuni Buddha, and together they formed ten thousand characters.

In this way, throughout the infinitely past buddha-fields of the ten directions—where the people everywhere speak various and different languages—they all together called upon the name and the title of Śākyamuni Buddha.
In each and every Buddha-field, there are ten billion words.
From the time Śākyamuni Buddha first began his practice of the Way until now, such has been the manner of his instruction of disciples and contemporaries.
The Buddha emitted a radiance that first issued from the soles of his feet, illuminating the entire Buddha-field with supreme brilliance,
revealing ten billion Jambudvīpas in the south, ten billion great oceans, ten billion Sumeru mountains, and ten billion Cakravāḍa mountains.
To the east, ten billion gods of the Pūrvavideha heaven; to the west, ten billion gods of the Aparagoyānī heaven;
to the north, ten billion gods of the Uttarakuru heaven; ten billion gods of the Cāturmahārājika heaven; ten billion gods of the Trāyastriṃśa heaven;
ten billion gods of the Yāma heaven; ten billion gods of the Tuṣita heaven; and ten billion gods of the Nirmāṇarati-vaśavartin heaven.
Ten billion *paranirmita-vaśavartin* devas, ten billion Brahmā devas, ten billion *brahmakāyika* devas,
ten billion *brahmapurohita* devas, ten billion *mahābrahmā* devas, ten billion *parīttābha* devas,
ten billion *apramāṇābha* devas, ten billion *ābhāsvara* devas.
Ten billion Brahmapurohita devas, ten billion Brahmapārṣadya devas, ten billion Mahābrahmā devas, ten billion Parīttābha devas, ten billion Apramāṇābha devas, ten billion Ābhāsvara devas,
ten billion Parīttaśubha devas, ten billion Apramāṇaśubha devas, ten billion Śubhakṛtsna devas, ten billion Anabhraka devas, ten billion Puṇyaprasava devas, ten billion Bṛhatphala devas,
ten billion Avṛha devas, ten billion Atapa devas, ten billion Sudṛśa devas, ten billion Sudarśana devas, ten billion Akaniṣṭha devas... [ten billion] Śuddhāvāsa devas.
There are ten billion Yāma devas, ten billion Tuṣita devas, ten billion Nirmāṇarati devas,
ten billion Paranirmita-vaśavartin devas, ten billion Akaniṣṭha devas,
and ten billion Abhāsvara devas.
In this manner, each [light] illuminates and perceives the abodes where the various devas and humans dwell.
Throughout this entire Buddha-field, all are fully illuminated; this is the domain presided over by Śākyamuni Buddha.
In each of the ten directions, there are one hundred million small lands; each possesses its own great ocean and its own Mount Sumeru;
extending upward to the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, such is the extent of each individual small land.
There are ten billion small lands, which together constitute a single buddha-field named Kāśī.
The Buddha’s emanations have pervaded all ten billion small lands.
In each of these individual small lands there was a Buddha; in total, there were ten billion Buddhas, all of whom sat together with various bodhisattvas within those ten billion small lands.

All the devas and humans saw the Buddha; empowered by the Buddha’s majestic spiritual authority, all the bodhisattvas, devas, and humans looked at one another as if welcoming him, and they beheld the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī.

Furthermore, there were the Bodhisattva Mañjuśrī, the Bodhisattva Rāmaśrī, the Bodhisattva Dānaśrī, the Bodhisattva Guṇaśrī, the Bodhisattva Buddhaśrī, the Bodhisattva Nairaśrī, the Bodhisattva Viśvaśrī, the Bodhisattva Dhanaśrī, the Bodhisattva Bhadraśrī, and the Bodhisattva Dharmaśrī.
The Buddha-fields where these bodhisattvas reside are exceedingly delightful; each of those fields has its own distinct name:

the Buddha Ajñānapratyudgata, the Buddha Anilapratyudgata, the Buddha Aśatapratyudgata, the Buddha Aruṇapratyudgata, the Buddha Ajñātapatyudgata, the Buddha Utsannapratyudgata, the Buddha Indrapratyudgata, the Buddha Brahmāpatyudgata, and the Buddha Vīrapratyudgata.
The Sūtra on the Tuṣita Heaven Spoken by the Buddha (Buddhabhāṣita-tuṣita-sūtra)
